claims.public_status: implemented

claims.public_status: narrow Stage 2 checkpoint

claims.compatibility: Only the borrowed-`List` shape is promised; other ownership errors may still compile until the general pass lands.

negative_boundary.observation: Using a moved binding is refused at compile time.

claims.public_status: bounded host-C implementation
claims.bounded_capability: `extern` declarations and `repr(C)` layouts are honoured for the host C compiler only; no cross-ABI or cross-target promise is made.
claims.compatibility: Layout guarantees follow the host C compiler; changing compilers may change layout and is not a compatibility break in this profile.

positive_gate.observation: The C ABI profile builds and round-trips through host C.

negative_boundary.observation: Backends outside the host-C profile are recorded as unsupported with a stated reason.

claims.public_status: bounded Int Core: recursion and forward calls
claims.bounded_capability: User functions lower to C11 for the Int Core, including recursion and forward references. Other value types are outside the slice.
claims.compatibility: Emitted C11 is deterministic for the covered slice; the exact text is pinned by the Stage 2 gate.

positive_gate.observation: Int Core user-function calls lower and execute through C11.

negative_boundary.observation: Statements outside the lowered slice are refused with `E2S10` rather than mis-lowered.

claims.public_status: implemented for Core
claims.bounded_capability: Every Core `Int` operation is checked: overflow and non-representable results are refused or trapped, never wrapped.
claims.compatibility: The checked contract holds across every backend that claims the Core; a backend that cannot honour it must report unsupported.

positive_gate.observation: The numeric conformance corpus passes on every supported backend.

negative_boundary.observation: Operations that cannot be represented are refused or trapped rather than wrapping.

claims.public_status: Core only
claims.bounded_capability: `build`, `run`, `check` and `test` accept Core sources. Sources outside the Core are refused by the driver, not partially compiled.
claims.compatibility: Command names and exit statuses are stable; the accepted source set grows with the Core.

positive_gate.observation: Each subcommand succeeds on Core sources.

negative_boundary.observation: Non-Core sources produce a refusal outcome instead of a partial build.

claims.public_wording: Linux x86-64 native CLI application framework
claims.public_status: bounded direct-static implementation
claims.bounded_capability: The CLI framework produces a direct static Linux x86-64 binary for the declarative command profile. No dynamic linking or other host is covered.
claims.compatibility: Argument parsing and exit statuses are gated; the framework surface may grow between releases.

positive_gate.observation: The declarative CLI example builds statically and runs.

negative_boundary.observation: Targets outside Linux x86-64 are recorded as unsupported with a stated reason.

claims.public_status: implemented: nested-block and looping Int/Bool/Text Core
claims.bounded_capability: The Stage 1 seed is written in Kofun and kept beside a hand-audited C transliteration. Its line-oriented Core lowers checked Int arithmetic, six comparisons, Bool equality, Bool literals and bindings, unary `!`, short-circuiting `&&`/`||`, Text literals/concatenation/equality through a conditionally emitted allocation-list runtime, nested `if`/`else if`/`else` blocks whose bindings leave scope at their `}`, and `while`/`for NAME in A .. B` loops that nest with those blocks, evaluate each range end once, and scope the bound name to the loop body; `print` accepts Int or Text and the Core still has no assignment or non-main function declaration.
claims.compatibility: The pre-existing arithmetic, Bool, nested-block and loop corpora remain byte-identical because the Text runtime is emitted only for Text programs. The seed pair changes together, its digest records the change, and every corpus differentials both compiler paths.

positive_gate.observation: The Kofun seed and audited C transliteration emit byte-identical C for the arithmetic, Bool, nested-block, loop and Text corpora. The Text program compiles under the gate flags, executes escaped literals/concatenation/equality/printing, and retains no expression source; the older four C goldens remain byte-identical.

negative_boundary.observation: An `else` with no `if` to attach to exits nonzero and writes no C; twenty-eight adjacent typed-boundary, block-boundary, loop-boundary and Text-boundary fixtures are checked by the same gate.

claims.public_status: versioned oracle/backend observations for arithmetic plus focused grammar, value-if, match-guard, match-value, and enum-match families
claims.bounded_capability: Fuzzing is seeded and reproducible: the same seed yields the same programs and the same oracle/backend observations.
claims.compatibility: The observation protocol is versioned; a protocol change is a release-note event.

positive_gate.observation: Oracle and backend observations agree for every generated program.

negative_boundary.observation: A divergence between the oracle and a backend fails the gate with the differing program.

claims.public_status: checkpoint implemented
claims.bounded_capability: The backend writes a static ELF64 image directly, without an external assembler or linker, for the covered Core profiles.
claims.compatibility: Emitted images are byte-deterministic for a given source and target.

positive_gate.observation: A static ELF64 image is written and executes.

negative_boundary.observation: Corpora outside the lowered profiles are recorded as unsupported with a stated reason.

claims.public_status: bounded Stage 2 C11 slice with constructor-set exhaustiveness
claims.bounded_capability: Payload-free concrete enums match exhaustively over their constructor set. Payload-carrying and generic enums are outside the slice.
claims.compatibility: Exhaustiveness is checked for the covered shape; widening the shape is a release-note event.

positive_gate.observation: Payload-free enum matches lower and execute with exhaustiveness enforced.

negative_boundary.observation: Enum shapes outside the slice are refused rather than silently accepted.

claims.public_status: open

claims.compatibility: Nothing is promised; a future implementation arrives with its own claim and gate.

claims.compatibility: Nothing beyond the enumerated native checkpoints may be relied on.

claims.compatibility: Ownership errors outside the borrowed-`List` checkpoint may compile; that is a stated absence, not a regression.

claims.public_status: open
claims.bounded_capability: The active compiler is not a general parser or type checker. Only the enumerated Stage 2 checkpoints are claimed.
claims.compatibility: No general acceptance is promised; sources outside the checkpoints are refused.

claims.public_wording: Linux HTTP/1.1 epoll framework through C ABI
claims.public_status: bounded library implementation
claims.bounded_capability: A bounded HTTP/1.1 server library over epoll, reached through the C ABI profile. TLS, HTTP/2 and client redirects are outside it.
claims.compatibility: The request/response state machine is bounded and gated; resource limits may tighten between releases.

positive_gate.observation: The bounded HTTP/1.1 server accepts and answers gated requests.

negative_boundary.observation: Requests beyond the bounded state machine are refused rather than buffered without limit.

claims.public_status: bounded same-package `import a.b as local`; local-only `AliasBindingId` preserves target identity, with no public/per-name/external aliases or `bin/kofun` routing
claims.bounded_capability: Same-package `import a.b as local` only. The alias is local, never re-exported, and does not route the driver.
claims.compatibility: Alias identity is local-only; making an alias public is a release-note event.

positive_gate.observation: Same-package aliases resolve while preserving target identity.

negative_boundary.observation: Public, per-name and external aliases are outside the profile and are refused.

claims.public_status: same bounded Int Core lowered to AArch64; executed under `qemu-aarch64`
claims.bounded_capability: The same bounded Int Core lowers to AArch64. Execution evidence requires `qemu-aarch64`; without it the gate reports a skip rather than a pass.
claims.compatibility: AArch64 tracks the x86-64 Int Core profile; divergence would be a release-note event.

positive_gate.observation: AArch64 images are emitted and, with qemu present, execute to the expected values.

negative_boundary.observation: Without `qemu-aarch64` the execution branch is reported as skipped, never as passed.

claims.public_status: a `return` of a direct call branches instead of calling, so direct and mutual recursion in that position run in constant stack; proved by executing three million steps under a lowered stack limit
claims.bounded_capability: A `return` of a direct call becomes a branch, so recursion in tail position runs in constant stack. Calls in non-return position still consume stack.
claims.compatibility: The constant-stack property is promised only for a `return` of a direct call.

positive_gate.observation: Three million recursive steps complete under a lowered stack limit.

negative_boundary.observation: Calls outside return position remain ordinary calls and are bounded by the stack limit.

claims.public_status: literal magnitudes through `INT64_MAX`, backward-compatible deterministic encodings, and the complete signed range through checked expressions
claims.bounded_capability: Literals reach `INT64_MAX` and checked expressions reach the complete signed range, with deterministic encodings on both targets.
claims.compatibility: Encodings are backward compatible: a previously emitted image stays byte-identical unless a release note says otherwise.

positive_gate.observation: Int64 magnitudes and checked expressions emit deterministic encodings on both targets.

negative_boundary.observation: Values outside the representable range are refused or trapped, never wrapped.

claims.public_status: `//` and `%` use the specified floor semantics; `/` is not defined on `Int` and both targets refuse it with one diagnostic (#687); both guard zero and non-representable quotients with canonical per-operator `R010` diagnostics
claims.bounded_capability: `//` and `%` follow floor semantics on both targets. `/` is refused on `Int`, and zero or non-representable quotients trap with a canonical per-operator `R010`.
claims.compatibility: Floor semantics and the `R010` diagnostic identity are stable; the refusal of `/` on `Int` is deliberate and will not become a fallback.

positive_gate.observation: Floor division and remainder agree with the specification on both targets.

negative_boundary.observation: Division by zero and non-representable quotients trap with a canonical per-operator `R010` diagnostic.

claims.public_status: bounded compiler-shaped profile with parameters, locals, concatenation, forwarding, and direct calls

claims.public_status: bounded Int Core: six arguments, guarded returns, recursion

negative_boundary.observation: Corpora outside the Int Core profile are recorded as unsupported with a stated reason.

claims.public_status: bounded typed frontend only: declaration, labelled construction, typed reads, ownership and layout facts, and a scanner that produces and consumes `List[Token]`; no module, generic, or backend lowering

negative_boundary.observation: Generic records are refused explicitly instead of being accepted outside the bounded profile.

claims.public_status: bounded same-package `pub import` / `pub from`; non-widening `ExportBindingId` edges, 64-edge chains, 1,024 bindings/module and 65,536 edges/package, KIF export facts, and facade/canonical tooling paths
